Operator:  
Good morning, and welcome to the Global Consumer Brands Inc., or GCB, Q3 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. During the Q&A session, please press star then one on your touchtone phone if you would like to ask a question. To withdraw your question, press star then two. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations.

Alex Rivera:  
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss GCB's Q3 results. With me on the call are Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; John Ramirez, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Marketing Officer; Mike Patel, Chief Supply Chain Officer; Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Innovation Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking and are based on our current expectations and beliefs. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson.

Sarah Thompson:  
Thank you, Alex. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. GCB delivered a solid Q3, demonstrating the resilience of our brands and the strength of our team. We are navigating a dynamic environment and remain focused on executing our strategic priorities.

Our discussion today will cover overall financial performance including geographic splits between developed and emerging markets, organic sales growth including its decomposition into volume, price, and mix, gross margin expansion, new product launches and our innovation pipeline, capital expenditure plans, marketing activities, supply chain efficiencies, sustainability efforts, digital transformation, and our outlook for the remainder of the year.

I will now turn the call over to John Ramirez to provide more detail on our financial results.

John Ramirez:  
Thank you, Sarah. As Sarah mentioned, we delivered a solid quarter. Net sales were $3.8 billion, representing a 5% increase compared to the prior year or 7% on an organic constant-currency basis. Gross margin was 52.3%, up 120 basis points year-over-year, driven by supply chain optimization, procurement excellence, and manufacturing efficiencies. Operating income was $650 million. Diluted earnings per share were $1.25. We continue to manage our costs effectively and invest in our long-term growth initiatives.

Good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining our Q3 earnings call for Global Consumer Brands Inc., or GCB as many of you know us. Today, I'd like to dive deep into our geographic performance, breaking it out between developed and emerging markets—a critical lens for understanding our growth trajectory in this dynamic CPG landscape. As a reminder, we define developed markets as North America, Western Europe, Japan, and Australia—regions characterized by mature consumer bases, high penetration rates, and intense competition. Emerging markets encompass Latin America, Asia-Pacific excluding Japan, Eastern Europe, the Middle East, and Africa, where we're seeing rapid urbanization, rising middle classes, and significant whitespace opportunities.

Developed markets accounted for 58% of our portfolio, delivering $2.2 billion in sales—flat year-over-year on an organic basis. In contrast, emerging markets represented 42% and drove $1.6 billion, surging 18% organically. This divergence underscores a tale of two worlds: stability and premiumization in the developed world versus high-volume growth fueled by affordability and distribution expansion in emerging regions.

In developed markets, we're navigating a tougher macro environment—persistent inflation averaging 4-6% across North America and Europe, coupled with softening consumer sentiment as tracked by NielsenIQ consumer confidence indices. North America, our largest pocket at 32% of total sales, grew 1% organically, led by our Health & Wellness segment. Premium launches like our new PureHarvest organic snack bars—now available in 15,000 Walmart and Kroger doors—gained 12 points of market share in the better-for-you category, per IRI scan data. But volume pressures from value-seekers hit our core power brands like Zestify sodas, down 2% in shipment volumes as households traded down to private labels.

Europe, at 20% of sales, was flat organically, with Germany and the UK dragging due to energy costs and regulatory scrutiny on packaging sustainability. Our EcoClean laundry detergent line, reformulated with 30% recycled ocean plastics, helped us claw back 3 points of share in France against Unilever's Persil, but overall, pricing actions to offset 8% input cost inflation limited top-line momentum. Margins here held steady at 22.5%—a 50 basis point improvement YoY—thanks to our zero-based budgeting initiative and supply chain efficiencies from our new New Jersey distribution hub, which reduced logistics costs by 15%.

Strategically, we're leaning into premiumization and e-commerce. Digital sales in developed markets jumped 25% to 18% of total, powered by Amazon partnerships and our DTC platform, where subscription models for personal care items like GlowEssence skincare are retaining 40% of first-time buyers. Looking ahead, we expect low-single-digit growth here in FY24, with innovation pipelines focused on functional beverages—think collagen-infused waters targeting the $12 billion global RTD protein market, as projected by Euromonitor.

Shifting to emerging markets, this is where GCB's playbook is firing on all cylinders. Organic growth of 18% marked our strongest quarter in three years, outpacing category growth of 10-12% per Kantar Worldpanel data. Latin America led at 22% growth on $450 million in sales, despite a 15% FX headwind from the weakening Brazilian real. In Brazil, our VitaBurst affordable hydration packs—priced at just 50 cents per sachet—expanded distribution to 200,000 mom-and-pop stores via our JDE partnership, driving 25% volume uplift and 4 points of market share gain versus Coca-Cola's local brands.

Asia-Pacific, 15% of total sales, delivered 16% organic growth, with India shining at 28%. Here, our localized SpiceGlow shampoo, infused with turmeric and neem for the $8 billion ayurvedic haircare segment, captured 6% market share in rural markets through Project Shakti-like micro-entrepreneur networks—mirroring Hindustan Unilever's model but scaled digitally via WhatsApp commerce. China, however, tempered the region at 8% growth due to COVID lockdowns in select provinces, though our e-commerce penetration hit 35% on Tmall and JD.com, where QuickSip ready-to-drink teas outperformed Nestlé's Nescafé ready variants by 10 points.

Across emerging markets, gross margins expanded 120 basis points to 28.2%, benefiting from localized sourcing—e.g., palm oil from Indonesian smallholders reducing costs by 10%—and our Emerging Market Fast Lane initiative, which deploys AI-driven route optimization for last-mile delivery, cutting DSD expenses by 18% in Mexico. Challenges persist: currency volatility shaved 300 basis points off reported growth, and geopolitical tensions in the Middle East pressured Turkey volumes down 5%. But our hedging program covered 80% of exposures, stabilizing EPS impact.

Zooming out, the developed-emerging split highlights our balanced portfolio strategy: developed markets provide margin stability and cash flow for reinvestment—generating 70% of our free cash flow—while emerging markets fuel EPS accretion, contributing 55% of growth. Trends like health & wellness (up 15% globally) and sustainability (our ESG scores up 20 points on MSCI ratings) are universal, but execution differs: premium in developed, accessible formats like single-serve pouches in emerging.

We're doubling down with $500 million in capex for FY24, including a new ASEAN manufacturing facility for plant-based snacks and digital transformation via SAP S/4HANA to enable real-time pricing elasticity modeling. Competitively, we're gaining share versus P&G and Reckitt in 70% of markets, per Nielsen, through superior innovation velocity—12 new SKUs launched this quarter alone.

In summary, developed markets offer a defensive moat; emerging, our offense. We guide FY23 organic growth to 6-8%, with emerging markets pulling 15-20% and developed 1-3%.

Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. I'll now turn to our gross margin performance, which continues to be a cornerstone of our profitability story here at GCB. For the quarter, we delivered a consolidated gross margin of 52.3%, up 120 basis points year-over-year from 51.1% and 40 basis points sequentially from Q1's 51.9%. This marks our sixth consecutive quarter of gross margin expansion, underscoring the resilience of our CPG portfolio amid persistent macroeconomic headwinds.

Let me break this down by the key drivers, starting with the top-line and cost dynamics. Revenue grew 4.2% organically, driven by a healthy 2.8% price/mix benefit—our precision pricing engine, which we've rolled out across 70% of our SKU base, allowed us to capture value without meaningful volume erosion. This was particularly evident in our North American Snacks segment, where we implemented targeted elasticities on brands like our flagship Nova Crunch bars, achieving a 3.5% price realization while maintaining share in the $25 billion U.S. salty snacks category, per Nielsen data.

Offsetting this, COGS inflation remained sticky at around 5-6% headline, largely from elevated commodity costs. Cocoa prices surged 45% year-to-date on supply constraints in Côte d'Ivoire and Ghana—issues mirroring those that hammered Hershey and Mondelez last year—impacting our chocolate-coated confections to the tune of 150 bps of margin pressure. Palm oil volatility added another 80 bps headwind, exacerbated by Indonesia's export restrictions, while dairy derivatives in our beverages unit faced 7% inflation from U.S. and EU milk powder tightness.

Yet, we more than offset these through our three-pillar productivity agenda, delivering $185 million in gross savings for the quarter, or 320 bps of margin accretion.

First, supply chain optimization accounted for 45% of savings. Our NovaLink digital platform, powered by AI-driven demand forecasting and integrated with SAP S/4HANA, reduced inventory levels by 12% while cutting logistics costs 8%. In Europe, where energy surcharges from the Ukraine conflict persist, we rerouted 20% of inbound freight through Turkey hubs, saving €15 million. This initiative is scaling globally, with pilots in our Personal Care segment targeting a further 5% freight reduction by year-end.

Second, procurement excellence made up 30% of savings. Forward contracts locked in 65% of our 2024 cocoa needs at 15% below spot, and our sustainable sourcing program with Rainforest Alliance suppliers yielded a 4% cost premium rebate on coffee for our Ready-to-Drink beverages. We're ahead of plan on our $1 billion procurement transformation, benchmarking against Unilever's model.

Third, manufacturing efficiencies contributed 25% of savings. Yield improvements from our Zero Loss factories—now at 92% OEE across 15 plants—drove 2.2% COGS reduction per unit. In Asia-Pacific, where we expanded capacity for our NovaGlow skincare line amid 10% category growth, automation upgrades cut conversion costs by 11%.

Regionally, the picture is mixed but encouraging. North America led with 54.2% margins, up 180 bps YoY, fueled by premiumization—our organic tea and plant-based yogurt SKUs, inspired by Chobani's success, shifted mix favorably by 200 bps. EMEA lagged at 49.8%, down 50 bps due to 12% energy inflation and soft demand in Germany, but sequential improvement reflects our 4% pricing actions on household essentials like our NovaClean detergents. Latin America held steady at 51.5%, with Brazil's inflation environment enabling 5.2% price hikes on snacks, while Asia-Pacific expanded to 53.1% on strong Indonesia palm efficiency gains despite China's zero-COVID supply disruptions.

Strategically, we're positioning for sustained 100-150 bps annual expansion through 2025. Key levers include portfolio reshaping: accelerating divestitures of low-margin legacy brands like our regional canned soups while doubling down on high-GM categories like beauty and nutrition, targeting 55%+ group margins long-term, akin to Colgate-Palmolive's trajectory. Sustainability-linked savings from our net-zero by 2040 roadmap include regenerative agriculture deals with farmers in Brazil for soy and corn, projecting 3-5% input cost reductions over three years. FX and hedge impacts: a stronger USD shaved 30 bps, but our 80% hedge coverage at favorable rates mitigated this.

Looking ahead, we guide to full-year gross margins of 52.5-52.8%, assuming mid-single-digit commodity inflation and no further geopolitical shocks. This embeds $750 million in productivity, positioning us to lap tough comps while funding 8-10% EPS growth.

Good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining our Q3 earnings call for Global Consumer Brands, or GCB as many of you know us. Today, I'd like to dive deeply into the decomposition of our organic sales growth—volume, price, and mix—which totaled +5.2%. This breakdown underscores the strength of our Revenue Growth Management, or RGM, playbook, where we captured +2.1% from volume, +1.8% from pricing actions, and +1.3% from favorable mix shift.

Starting with volume, we grew +2.1%, outpacing the total CPG category, which per NielsenIQ data declined -0.8% in measured channels globally. This reflects our focus on consumer-centric innovation and flawless execution at retail. Our core power brands drove +2.8% volume growth, gaining 110 basis points of market share in North America alone. Tide Pods benefited from our Eco-Refill pod launch, a recyclable cartridge system that resonated with sustainability-focused Gen Z and millennial households, boosting household penetration by 3.2 points in IRI-tracked channels.

New product initiatives contributed +1.4 points to volume. We launched 17 innovations this quarter, including our plant-based Dawn Powerwash spray in Europe, which captured +15% share in the dish care segment within four weeks of rollout, and a zero-sugar Gatorade variant in Latin America that drove +22% trial rates via TikTok sampling campaigns. E-commerce velocity remains a tailwind, with +12% volume growth on platforms like Amazon and Instacart, fueled by our Subscribe & Save bundles. In brick-and-mortar, we added 45,000 facings globally, including priority shelf space at Kroger and Tesco through targeted trade spend optimization.

Regionally, Emerging Markets were the star, growing +4.5% volume on robust GDP tailwinds and urbanization trends in India and Brazil. North America volume was flat at +0.2%, pressured by downtrading to private labels amid 3.5% grocery inflation, but we offset this with premium SKUs. Europe lagged at +1.1%, hit by weak fabric care demand, though Beauty volumes rebounded +3.2% post-summer travel recovery.

Pricing contributed +1.8%, balancing elasticity management with value communication. Headline grocery inflation cooled to +2.1% globally per Kantar, but our input costs—resins, palm oil, and energy—rose +4% sequentially due to Red Sea disruptions and El Niño weather impacts on ag commodities. We implemented modest, targeted hikes averaging +3.2% on 65% of our portfolio, focusing on low-elasticity categories like baby care (+4.1%) and oral care (+3.8%). In Grooming, Gillette Fusion5 ProGlide pricing held firm with minimal pushback, as consumers traded up for superior glide performance.

Our proprietary consumer panels showed average price elasticity of -1.8 across categories, better than the -2.2 industry benchmark. This discipline recaptured 85% of our $450 million in input cost inflation, protecting gross margins at 53.2%. Regionally, Emerging Markets pricing was +3.5%, leveraging aspirational pricing power in mid-tier urban segments. North America was more tempered at +1.2%, reflecting competitive dynamics with Dollar General's private labels, while Europe pricing came in at +1.9%, aided by list-price harmonization post-Brexit.

Favorable mix added +1.3%, driven by our Premiumize or Rationalize strategy, where we divested $200 million in low-single-digit growth SKUs last year and doubled down on high-margin platforms. Consumers gravitated to super-premium tiers, up +8.2% in sales weight. Examples: SK-II luxury skincare grew +14% volume in Asia-Pacific, capturing affluent millennials, while our Bounty Advanced paper towels with quilted bamboo fibers gained +9% share in the U.S., appealing to eco-conscious families willing to pay a 25% premium.

Health & Wellness now represents 28% of sales, up from 24% YoY, fueled by Olly probiotic gummies (+25% growth) amid gut health trends. Conversely, we ceded low-margin fabric softener share to concentrates, improving mix by 40 bps. Regionally, North America mix was strongest at +1.8%, with premium Beauty and Personal Care offsetting volume softness. Emerging Markets added +1.1%, as middle-class expansion favored branded nutritionals over staples. Europe mix was +0.9%, boosted by plant-based dairy alternatives competing with Nestlé and Danone.

This decomposition highlights our RGM maturity: volume resilience through innovation, pricing to sustain margins, and mix for profitability. We've embedded zero-based budgeting and AI-driven assortment optimization in our trade terms, targeting +200 bps of operating leverage in FY24. Looking ahead, we expect Q4 organic growth of 4-6%, with volume accelerating +2.5% on holiday ramps and holiday exclusives like limited-edition Febreze car diffusers.

Good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining our Q4 earnings call for Global Consumer Brands, or GCB as many of you know us. Today, I'd like to dive deep into our organic sales growth, which remains the north star metric for our core business performance here in the CPG space. For those new to our calls, organic sales growth excludes the impacts of acquisitions, divestitures, and foreign exchange—purely reflecting our ability to grow volumes, optimize pricing, and shift mix toward higher-margin SKUs.

In Q4, we delivered organic sales growth of 4.8%, bringing our full-year organic growth to 5.1%. This marks our third consecutive year of 5%+ organic growth, outpacing the broader CPG industry average of around 2-3% as reported by NielsenIQ and IRI data. Compared to peers like Procter & Gamble's 4% or Unilever's 3.8% full-year organics, we're holding a clear share advantage, particularly in North American household and personal care categories.

Breaking it down by component—our Q4 organic growth was driven by 2.1% volume growth, 2.5% net pricing, and a 0.2% favorable mix shift. Volumes were the standout, rebounding from the softer Q3 we called out last quarter amid seasonal inventory destocking in mass channels. Pricing remained disciplined at 2.5%, below the 4-5% CPI inflation we've all been navigating, which underscores our commitment to value-for-money positioning—think our Everyday Essentials tier that gained 150 bps of market share in discount channels.

Full-year volumes grew 1.8%, with pricing at 2.9% and mix adding 0.4%. Mix was boosted by premiumization trends: sales of our high-margin PureVital plant-based beverages and EcoGlow sustainable skincare lines grew 12% organically, now representing 18% of total sales, up from 14% last year. This mirrors the industry shift we're seeing, where consumers are trading up selectively—McKinsey's latest CPG report pegs premium segment growth at 8-10% globally versus flat core volumes.

North America, our largest market at 55% of sales, posted 6.2% organic growth in Q4 and 6.8% full-year. This was fueled by distribution gains—we expanded ACV to 98% in key snack categories like our CrunchMax bars, adding 1.2 points of velocity through targeted in-store merchandising and Club store resets with Costco and Sam's Club. Health & wellness drove 40% of the increment here, with NARTD beverages up 9%, outpacing category growth amid Ozempic-related appetite suppression headwinds that have softened indulgent snacks industry-wide.

In Europe, we saw 3.5% Q4 organics on 4.2% full-year, price-led as expected given 6-7% regional inflation. Volumes were flat, but we gained 80 bps share in fabric care via our CleanWave hypoallergenic pods, capitalizing on Unilever's pricing backlash in the UK. Regulatory tailwinds from the EU Green Deal helped our sustainable packaging initiatives, with 25% of European SKUs now recyclable—driving loyalty among Gen Z shoppers.

Latin America was our growth engine at 8.4% Q4 and 9.1% full-year, led by Brazil and Mexico. Volumes surged 5.2% on economic recovery and our VitaBoost functional foods, which captured 2 points of share in the growing fortified dairy segment. Pricing was moderated to 3%, balancing affordability with margin protection amid volatile commodity costs like cocoa and palm oil.

Asia-Pacific delivered 5.7% Q4 and 6.3% full-year, with China e-commerce channels growing 15% via Tmall and JD.com partnerships. India volumes popped 7% on rural distribution expansion—we added 50,000 villages through Project Shakti, our micro-entrepreneur program, mirroring Hindustan Unilever's playbook but with faster ROI.

Strategically, these results reflect three key initiatives we've accelerated. First, innovation velocity: We launched 22 new products in 2023, with 70% hitting $50M+ run rates—ahead of our 60% target. Standouts include the FlexFuel zero-sugar energy drinks, which achieved 20% repeat purchase rates in the first six months.

Second, digital and omnichannel acceleration: E-commerce now 22% of sales, up 400 bps YoY, with AI-driven personalization boosting conversion 15% on our D2C site. We're leveraging tools like Profitero's shelf analytics to optimize everyday low pricing in Walmart and Kroger.

Third, supply chain resilience: Post-2022 disruptions, our S&OP tech stack—powered by SAP IBP and AI forecasting—reduced stockouts to 2.5% from 5%, enabling those volume gains. We're also hedging 80% of 2024 commodity exposure, mitigating risks from El Niño-driven ag volatility.

Looking forward, we guide 2024 organic growth of 4-6%, with volumes inflecting positive early. Risks include persistent inflation eroding low-income consumer wallets—we've stress-tested scenarios down to 2% volumes—but tailwinds from premium health trends and China stimulus should support the midpoint.

Thank you, Sarah. I'll now turn to our outlook for the fourth quarter and full fiscal year 2025, with a particular focus on organic sales growth. As you know, organic sales represent our core business performance, excluding the impacts of acquisitions, divestitures, and foreign exchange. This metric has been a hallmark of our disciplined execution in the CPG landscape, where we've consistently outperformed peers like Procter & Gamble and Unilever amid persistent inflation headwinds and shifting consumer behaviors.

For Q4, we are guiding to organic sales growth of 3% to 5%. This reflects a sequential acceleration from Q3's 2.5% print, driven by a healthy blend of pricing discipline and modest volume recovery. Pricing is expected to contribute 2 to 3 points, as we lap last year's aggressive hikes and hold steady on everyday low pricing strategies in high-velocity categories like household care and snacks. Volume growth should add 1 to 2 points, fueled by share gains in North America, where our SnackJoy portfolio—led by the reformulated JoyBites low-sugar bars—continues to steal 20 basis points of market share per recent IRI scan data, outpacing private label encroachment.

Looking to full FY 2025, our organic sales growth guidance is 4% to 6%, positioning us at the high end of our long-term 3-5% algorithm while navigating a macro environment reminiscent of the post-COVID stabilization phase. This implies roughly flat-to-1% volume growth offset by 3-5% price/mix tailwinds.

Our growth algorithm remains anchored in three pillars: innovation-led volume, premiumization via price/mix, and operational agility. Innovation, at 30% of incremental sales: We're launching 15+ SKUs across our portfolio, including the PureSip Hydrate+ functional beverage line with electrolytes and adaptogens, targeting the $12B RTD hydration market growing at 8% CAGR per Euromonitor. Early tests in APAC show 15% trial rates, echoing the success of our FreshGlow EcoClean detergent pods, which drove 12% category growth last year.

Price/Mix, 50% of growth: Expect 3-4% from continued premium shifts—think 20%+ margins on our up-tiered personal care lines like GlowEssence serums—while defending value tiers against discounters like Aldi and Lidl. Our dynamic pricing AI, powered by Salesforce Einstein and integrated with NielsenIQ POS data, has optimized 85% of our SKU portfolio, reducing stockouts by 25% and enabling real-time elasticity modeling.

Volume Recovery, 20%: Volumes should inflect positive as pantry-loading fades and at-home consumption normalizes. Health and wellness trends are key, with our SnackJoy CleanLabel nuts capturing Gen Z spend amid a 5% category contraction for indulgent snacks.

North America, 50% of sales, 4-6% organic growth: Strongest performer, with 2% volume upside from distribution wins at Walmart and Kroger. Pricing stabilizes at +3%, but trade-down pressures in mass channels cap upside—our EDLP initiatives have held dollar share flat versus last year.

Europe/MEA, 25% of sales, 3-5% growth: Moderating inflation supports 1-2% volumes, bolstered by our Unilever-competitive sustainability play: 100% recyclable packaging on FreshGlow by Q1, aligning with EU Green Deal regs and driving 10% loyalty lift per Kantar data. Turkey and South Africa remain FX headwinds but offset by 7% growth in UK grocery.

Asia-Pacific/LatAm, 25% of sales, 4-7% growth: High-teens volume in India and Brazil from urban expansion—PureSip entering 5,000 Reliance Retail doors—and e-commerce surge via Shopee/Tokopedia, now 18% of APAC sales (up from 12%). Pricing +4% reflects aspirational consumer shifts, though China softness (1% growth) tempers the region due to zero-COVID hangover.

This guidance embeds our Resilient Growth Framework, including $200M in supply chain savings from GenAI-optimized forecasting (reducing raw ag input volatility, e.g., cocoa up 40% YTD) and $150M from direct-to-consumer channels via Shopify Plus. We're also accelerating M&A tuck-ins, like the recent $300M bolt-on in plant-based snacks, but these are ex-organic.

Risks include persistent inflation pass-through (e.g., palm oil +15%), potential U.S. recessionary trade-down (monitoring DMI basket data), and competitive intensity from Nestlé's Vitality line. Upside levers: faster-than-expected volume snapback if Fed cuts materialize, or share gains from our 50/50 volume/price balance versus peers' pricing-heavy models.

In summary, we're confident in delivering 3-5% Q4 and 4-6% FY25 organic growth, underscoring our category leadership and execution edge. This sets us up for margin expansion to 22-23% and 8-10% EPS growth.

Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. As we wrap up our Q3 and full-year results here at Global Consumer Brands Inc., or GCB, I'd like to dive into our capital expenditure—or Capex—plans and priorities for 2024 and beyond. This is a critical lever for driving sustainable growth in our CPG portfolio, which spans high-velocity snacks like our flagship NutriCrunch bar line, plant-based beverages under the GreenWave brand, and premium personal care products akin to what you've seen from leaders like P&G and Unilever.

In FY2023, we deployed $825 million in Capex, representing about 3.8% of our net sales—up 18% from $700 million in FY2022, and squarely in line with our long-term target range of 3-4% of sales. This uptick reflects our deliberate shift toward resilience and growth post the supply chain disruptions we've all navigated since 2020. For context, that's comparable to peers like Colgate-Palmolive's ~3.5% Capex intensity or PepsiCo's disciplined 3-4% band, allowing us to fund high-ROI projects without compromising our industry-leading 25%+ EBITDA margins.

Looking ahead to FY2024, we're guiding Capex to $900 million, or roughly 3.9% of projected sales, with a multi-year outlook through 2026 holding steady at $2.8-3.2 billion cumulatively. This isn't spend for spend's sake—every dollar is tied to our three strategic pillars: capacity for premiumization, supply chain digitization and automation, and sustainability leadership.

First, manufacturing capacity expansion—40% of our 2024 Capex, or ~$360 million. We're prioritizing high-growth SKUs amid the CPG premiumization trend, where consumers are trading up to health-focused and sustainable options. For instance, our NutriCrunch plant-based protein bars saw 22% volume growth in 2023, outpacing the 8% category average per Nielsen data. To support this, we're investing $150 million in a new greenfield facility in the U.S. Midwest—think states like Ohio, mirroring P&G's smart factory playbook in Greensboro. This 300,000 sq ft plant will add 20% capacity for extruded snacks and incorporate Industry 4.0 tech from Day 1, including ABB robotics for 30% faster changeovers between SKUs.

Regionally, North America gets 55% of this bucket at $200 million, fueling e-commerce fulfillment for Amazon and DTC channels, where our online sales mix hit 18% of total in Q3—double Unilever's pace in some categories. In APAC, a $100 million brownfield upgrade in Vietnam targets the booming plant-based dairy alternatives, capturing the 15% CAGR in that market per Euromonitor. EMEA rounds it out with $60 million for hygiene products in Eastern Europe, hedging inflation pressures.

Second, supply chain and distribution—25% of Capex, or $225 million. Inflation and freight volatility have been brutal—our COGS rose 6% YoY in 2023 despite hedging—but we're countering with next-gen logistics. A key initiative is $120 million for three automated micro-fulfillment centers in high-density U.S. metros like Atlanta, Chicago, and LA. Partnering with Ocado or Swisslog tech, these will slash last-mile costs by 25% and boost OTIF delivery to 98% from 92%, critical as grocery e-comm grows at 12% annually.

We're also rolling out SAP S/4HANA ERP upgrades across 80% of our network by year-end, integrating AI-driven demand sensing from Blue Yonder. This mirrors Mondelez's playbook, where similar tech cut inventory by 15% and working capital by 10%. Regionally, LatAm sees $50 million for cold-chain resilience in Brazil, addressing perishables like our GreenWave juices amid El Niño weather risks.

Third, digital transformation and R&D—20% of Capex, or $180 million. CPG is going digital or dying—our consumer data platform, powered by Snowflake and AWS, processed 50 petabytes last year, enabling personalized marketing that lifted repeat purchase rates 12%. We're allocating $90 million to AI/ML for predictive maintenance and dynamic pricing, targeting 5-7% gross margin expansion. In R&D, $50 million funds our Innovation Hubs in Boston and Singapore, accelerating low/no-cal sweeteners and upcycled ingredients—think turning food waste into NutriCrunch fibers, aligning with Nestlé's regenerative ag goals.

Finally, sustainability and resilience—15% of Capex, or $135 million. ESG isn't optional; it's table stakes. We're hitting 100% renewable energy in North American plants by 2025 via $60 million in solar and wind PPAs, cutting Scope 2 emissions 40% and energy costs 15%. Water stewardship gets $40 million for zero-liquid-discharge systems at five sites, vital in water-stressed APAC. And $35 million bolsters nearshoring with backup suppliers in Mexico, reducing China exposure by 30% post-COVID.

Strategically, these investments yield strong returns: our IRR hurdle is 15-20%, with 2023 projects already delivering 18% blended. Payback periods average 3-4 years, funding 60% via operating cash flow—our free cash flow conversion hit 95% in 2023. We're flexible, too: 20% of Capex is contingency-proof, scalable based on volume ramps or M&A like our recent bolt-on in premium oral care.

In summary, this Capex blueprint positions GCB to outgrow the CPG industry at 5-7% organically through 2026, while de-risking the balance sheet—net debt to EBITDA stays at 2.2x. We're not just building factories; we're building the future of consumer goods.

Following my remarks, Lisa Chen will provide an update on our marketing and brand performance.

Lisa Chen:  
Thank you, John. We continue to see strong performance across our key brands. Our marketing investments are driving increased consumer engagement, and we are particularly pleased with the results of our recent PureHarvest campaign. This campaign leveraged targeted digital ads and in-store activations to boost awareness of our organic snack lines, resulting in a 15% uplift in household penetration and sustained share gains against competitors.

After me, Mike Patel will discuss our supply chain initiatives.

Mike Patel:  
Thank you, Lisa. Our focus remains on optimizing our supply chain to enhance efficiency and resilience. We are implementing advanced analytics to improve forecasting and inventory management, which has already reduced stockouts by 25% and logistics costs through AI route optimization. Our Emerging Market Fast Lane and NovaLink platforms are key, delivering significant savings while scaling globally.

Finally, Dr. Elena Vasquez will share insights on our innovation pipeline.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:  
Thank you, Mike. We are excited about the progress we are making on our new product development initiatives. Our pipeline is robust, and we are confident that our innovations will drive future growth. Our recent product, VitalEats Plant-Powered Protein Bar, is showing promising early results.
